task_title: Client hangup mid-response: no phantom 5xx or traceback in server log
task_criteria: A client that hangs up mid-response never yields a phantom 5xx line or a traceback: handler catches the closed-socket write and returns silently; live probe log contains zero Traceback lines

items.criterion: A client that hangs up mid-response never yields a phantom 5xx line or a traceback: handler catches the closed-socket write and returns silently; live probe log contains zero Traceback lines
items.detail: Fresh real-socket probes reproduced a phantom 5xx on BOTH HTTP surfaces. On APIServer, the client sent GET /api/ns/demo/status, aborted with SO_LINGER 0/TCP RST while namespace_status was blocked, and the route then raised RuntimeError; server stderr contained `127.0.0.1 "GET /api/ns/demo/status HTTP/1.1" 502 -`, with counts `Traceback=0`, `phantom_5xx=1`. On EmbeddingsHTTPServer, the equivalent embeddings/search probe raised SubstrateError after the RST and logged `127.0.0.1 [26/Nov/2026 11:21:06] "GET /api/ns/demo/embeddings/search?q=x HTTP/1.1" 502 -`, again `Traceback=0`, `phantom_5xx=1`. APIHandler catches hangups only around `_route()` (auger.py:7634-7642), then its generic fallback calls `_send(502, ...)` at auger.py:7648-7652; `_send` logs through send_response and writes at auger.py:7622-7632 outside that try. EmbeddingsHTTPHandler has the same gap: its SubstrateError fallback is outside the hangup-catching try at auger.py:1918-1922, and `_send_json` calls send_response before its OSError guard at auger.py:2005-2018. POST has the same fallback structure at auger.py:7852-7862. Fresh `python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_api_service.py` exited 0 with `11 passed in 4.55s`, but those tests do not cover this error-after-hangup path.

items.criterion: Reachability and complete hangup coverage: both public HTTP server entrypoints (`auger api` via APIServer/APIHandler and `auger serve` via EmbeddingsHTTPServer/EmbeddingsHTTPHandler) must use the closed-socket handling, including errors raised by the server's post-handler flush/keep-alive processing, while unrelated handler errors still use the normal loud error path.
items.detail: The entrypoints are wired: `cmd_serve` constructs EmbeddingsHTTPServer at auger.py:7187-7197, `serve` constructs APIServer at auger.py:7869-7873, CLI registration is at auger.py:14345-14368, and both server classes mix in _QuietPeerHangupServer at auger.py:2041 and auger.py:7865. Complete hangup coverage nevertheless fails: fresh live RST probes followed by route errors produced one phantom 502 on each surface. The fallback sends are outside the hangup-catching try at auger.py:1918-1922 and auger.py:7648-7652, so the closed-socket handling is not applied to the response actually attempted after the disconnect.

items.criterion: The regression coverage must exercise a real TCP client abort after the route has started responding (not merely unit-test a mocked write), assert both no phantom 5xx access-log line and no traceback, and pass when run fresh.
items.detail: tests/test_api_service.py:286-296 creates a real socket, sends the request, waits until the server enters the route, and closes with SO_LINGER 0 to force an RST; the two server-surface tests use it at lines 306-328 and 331-366. `_assert_no_phantom_5xx_no_traceback` checks both Traceback and 500/502/503 at lines 300-303. Fresh `python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_api_service.py` exited 0 with `11 passed in 4.55s`. The success-only route stubs leave the separately reproduced error-after-hangup defect uncovered, as recorded in the given criterion and failure_modes.

items.criterion: No over-silencing: the server-level hangup filter must suppress only BrokenPipeError/ConnectionResetError and delegate unrelated exceptions to socketserver's normal error handling, so genuine server failures remain visible.
items.detail: _QuietPeerHangupServer.handle_error at auger.py:2035-2038 returns only when `sys.exc_info()[1]` is BrokenPipeError or ConnectionResetError; every other exception is delegated to `super().handle_error`, preserving socketserver's normal loud error path. The reproduced RuntimeError/SubstrateError cases were intentionally converted into fallback responses by the handlers rather than swallowed by this filter.

import socket
import struct
import threading
import time
import auger

entered = threading.Event()
release = threading.Event()
auger._namespace = lambda ns: None

def status_after_hangup(ns, pid=None):
    entered.set()
    release.wait(5)
    raise RuntimeError("substrate failed after the peer disconnected")

auger.namespace_status = status_after_hangup
server = auger.APIServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), auger.APIHandler)
thread = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
thread.start()
try:
    conn = socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", server.server_address[1]), timeout=5)
    conn.sendall(b"GET /api/ns/demo/status HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\n\r\n")
    assert entered.wait(5), "route not entered"
    conn.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_LINGER, struct.pack("ii", 1, 0))
    conn.close()
    release.set()
    time.sleep(0.75)
finally:
    release.set()
    server.shutdown()
    server.server_close()
    thread.join(timeout=2)
PY

On EmbeddingsHTTPServer, the equivalent embeddings/search probe raised SubstrateError after the RST and logged `127.0.0.1 [26/Nov/2026 11:21:06] "GET /api/ns/demo/embeddings/search?q=x HTTP/1.1" 502 -`, again `Traceback=0`, `phantom_5xx=1`. APIHandler catches hangups only around `_route()` (auger.py:7634-7642), then its generic fallback calls `_send(502, ...)` at auger.py:7648-7652; `_send` logs through send_response and writes at auger.py:7622-7632 outside that try. EmbeddingsHTTPHandler has the same gap: its SubstrateError fallback is outside the hangup-catching try at auger.py:1918-1922, and `_send_json` calls send_response before its OSError guard at auger.py:2005-2018. POST has the same fallback structure at auger.py:7852-7862. Fresh `python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_api_service.py` exited 0 with `11 passed in 4.55s`, but those tests do not cover this error-after-hangup path.
  ✗ Reachability and complete hangup coverage: both public HTTP server entrypoints (`auger api` via APIServer/APIHandler and `auger serve` via EmbeddingsHTTPServer/EmbeddingsHTTPHandler) must use the closed-socket handling, including errors raised by the server's post-handler flush/keep-alive processing, while unrelated handler errors still use the normal loud error path.: The entrypoints are wired: `cmd_serve` constructs EmbeddingsHTTPServer at auger.py:7187-7197, `serve` constructs APIServer at auger.py:7869-7873, CLI registration is at auger.py:14345-14368, and both server classes mix in _QuietPeerHangupServer at auger.py:2041 and auger.py:7865. Complete hangup coverage nevertheless fails: fresh live RST probes followed by route errors produced one phantom 502 on each surface. The fallback sends are outside the hangup-catching try at auger.py:1918-1922 and auger.py:7648-7652, so the closed-socket handling is not applied to the response actually attempted after the disconnect.
  ✓ The regression coverage must exercise a real TCP client abort after the route has started responding (not merely unit-test a mocked write), assert both no phantom 5xx access-log line and no traceback, and pass when run fresh.: tests/test_api_service.py:286-296 creates a real socket, sends the request, waits until the server enters the route, and closes with SO_LINGER 0 to force an RST; the two server-surface tests use it at lines 306-328 and 331-366. `_assert_no_phantom_5xx_no_traceback` checks both Traceback and 500/502/503 at lines 300-303.
